free_tier.stated: Free: at most 1,000 items, of which at most 50 may be non-public. Pro (paid): unlimited storage, full-res uploads with no monthly cap; $11 per month, $82 per year or $148 per two years in domestic USD (third-party price report).
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered for public images (staticflickr.com CDN). Non-public content on free accounts is capped at 50 and at risk of deletion, so egress is real only for public photos.

tooling: Flickr API (OAuth1), flickr-sync; no native rclone backend; ShareX and Lightroom publish plugins.
chaining: Unlimited free accounts x 1,000 items. This is a per-record cap, not a byte cap. But 1,000 items x 200 MB max = ~200 GB/account at absolute best, and item 1,001 is deleted.
limits_note: 1,000 items; 50 non-public items; free accounts limited to Safe content and no commercial use. 'Upload over 1,000 items' is explicitly prohibited and 'Content that exceeds these limits is at risk of suspension or deletion'.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Enforcement is real and documented: over-limit accounts are suspended or have content deleted. Pro is required for any bulk use.

extras.agent_focus: image hosts and photo platforms as bulk binary storage: free byte ceilings are high or unlimited because photos are the product, but most re-encode. Crux = which hosts return the original bytes, verified by HEAD/hash, not by marketing copy.
